topic: What happens if you run a marathon?
title: What running a marathon does
hook: What happens if you run a marathon?

beats.label: 5 MI
beats.line: Five miles in, your heart rate climbs and breathing quickens.

beats.label: 13 MI
beats.line: By mile thirteen, your heart pumps harder to hold pace.

beats.label: 20 MI
beats.line: Around mile twenty, stored glycogen runs low, and you hit the wall.

beats.label: 24 MI
beats.line: By mile twenty-four, heavy sweat can leave you dehydrated.

beats.label: 26 MI
beats.line: At the finish, sore muscles remind you of every mile.

end.line: Would you ever run a full marathon?

description: How your heart, energy stores and muscles react as marathon miles add up.

facts.claim: During prolonged exercise, heart rate and breathing rate rise to deliver more oxygen to muscles.
Stored muscle glycogen can run low around mile 18 to 20, a state runners call 'hitting the wall'.
Heavy sweating during endurance exercise causes fluid loss and can lead to dehydration if not replaced.
Muscle soreness after prolonged exercise is common and usually eases within a few days.
